**Joseph Arthur Mazzulla** (born June 30, 1988) is an American professional [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") coach who is the head coach for the [Boston Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics") of the [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA). He played [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") for the [West Virginia Mountaineers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_Mountaineers_men's_basketball "West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball") as a [point guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_guard "Point guard").
Following his collegiate career, Mazzulla went undrafted in the [2011 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NBA_draft "2011 NBA draft"), and chose to pursue a career in coaching at the college level. He coached at [Glenville State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenville_State_University "Glenville State University") and [Fairmont State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairmont_State_University "Fairmont State University") as an assistant coach for three seasons each before being hired to be an assistant coach for the [Maine Red Claws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine_Red_Claws "Maine Red Claws") in 2016. In 2017, Mazzulla was rehired at Fairmont State, this time as their basketball program's head coach. After these stints of coaching at the collegiate level and in the [NBA D-League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_G_League "NBA G League"), he joined the Celtics as an assistant coach in 2019.
In September 2022, Mazzulla was named the interim head coach of the Celtics after head coach [Ime Udoka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ime_Udoka "Ime Udoka") was suspended for the entire season. Mazzulla was named the full-time head coach in February 2023 after leading the team to a league-best 42–17 record at the [NBA All-Star break](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_All-Star_break "NBA All-Star break"). In his second season, Mazzulla led the Celtics to a league-best 64 wins and an [NBA Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals "2024 NBA Finals"). He currently holds the highest winning percentage of any coach in NBA history with over 200 games coached.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-4) Mazzulla is also the youngest head coach to win the [NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Finals "NBA Finals") since [Bill Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Russell "Bill Russell") did so in [1969](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_NBA_Finals "1969 NBA Finals") as a player-coach and is the ninth-youngest head coach to win the Finals in NBA history.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-youngest_coach-5)
Mazzulla has been noted in both NBA media and in general for his eccentric attitudes towards the game, his players, and the wins and losses he faces, leading some to nickname him **Psycho Joe**.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-6)
## Early life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Mazzulla&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]
[![Joe Mazzulla playing basketball at Bishop Hendricken High School in 2005](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Joe_Mazzulla_playing_basketball_in_the_division_l_high_school_state_championship_game_2005.jpg/250px-Joe_Mazzulla_playing_basketball_in_the_division_l_high_school_state_championship_game_2005.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Joe_Mazzulla_playing_basketball_in_the_division_l_high_school_state_championship_game_2005.jpg)Mazzulla in 2005
Joseph Mazzulla was born to [Daniel Mazzulla Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Mazzulla "Dan Mazzulla"), an Italian American, and Latresa Mazzulla, an African American, on June 30, 1988, in [Johnston, Rhode Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnston,_Rhode_Island "Johnston, Rhode Island").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-8) He attended [Bishop Hendricken High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bishop_Hendricken_High_School "Bishop Hendricken High School") in Rhode Island, making the all-state first team.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-furfari-9) Mazzulla won three state titles as a [point guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_guard "Point guard") at Bishop Hendricken, with his third as a senior on a last-second shot.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-thamel-10) As a senior, Mazzulla was injured in a car accident, sustaining no major injuries.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-11)
## College career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Mazzulla&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: College career")]
As a freshman at [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Virginia_Mountaineers_men's_basketball "West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball"), Mazzulla helped the team win the [2007 National Invitation Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_National_Invitation_Tournament "2007 National Invitation Tournament") under coach [John Beilein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Beilein "John Beilein").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-furfari-9)
In the [2008 NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2008 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), Mazzulla posted 13 points, 11 rebounds, and eight assists in a second-round upset of [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_Blue_Devils_men's_basketball "Duke Blue Devils men's basketball"). He was forced to [redshirt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redshirt_\(college_sports\) "Redshirt \(college sports\)") the [2008–09 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_season "2008–09 NCAA Division I men's basketball season") due to a shoulder injury against [Ole Miss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ole_Miss_Rebels_men's_basketball "Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball"), as his growth plate never fused with his shoulder.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-thamel-10) Mazzulla was unsure if he would ever play again, but practiced for two hours a day and underwent surgery to make a comeback.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-12)
In April 2009, Mazzulla was arrested for domestic battery at a bar in [Morgantown, West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgantown,_West_Virginia "Morgantown, West Virginia"), and was suspended by coach [Bob Huggins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Huggins "Bob Huggins").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-thamel-10) Around this time, Mazzulla received a phone call from Mountaineer legend [Jerry West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_West "Jerry West"). West criticized Mazzulla for failing to live up to expectations and pleaded with him not to waste his talents any longer. Mazzulla credits this call for helping to set him on the right path.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-13)
As a redshirt junior, Mazzulla was named a captain and helped West Virginia reach the [2010 Final Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Final_Four "2010 Final Four"), where the Mountaineers lost to eventual champion [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Duke_Blue_Devils_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team"). In the game prior, he scored a then-career-high 17 points in the Elite Eight upset of [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kentucky_Wildcats_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-fenton-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-15)
As a senior, Mazzulla averaged 7.7 points and 3.8 rebounds per game.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-gaz-16)
In his collegiate career, Mazzulla recorded 700 points and 340 assists.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-jackson-17)
## Coaching career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Mazzulla&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Coaching career")]
### College coaching career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Mazzulla&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: College coaching career")]
Shortly after graduating from college, Mazzulla was offered a coaching job at [Nova Southeastern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nova_Southeastern_Sharks "Nova Southeastern Sharks") but turned it down to pursue professional playing opportunities.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-18) He joined [Glenville State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenville_State_Pioneers "Glenville State Pioneers") as an assistant in September 2011 after he was unable to find any professional playing opportunities.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-19)
In 2013, Mazzulla was hired as an assistant at [Fairmont State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairmont_State_Fighting_Falcons "Fairmont State Fighting Falcons") under [Jerrod Calhoun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerrod_Calhoun "Jerrod Calhoun").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-furfari-9) During the 2016–17 season, Mazzulla served as an assistant for the [Maine Red Claws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine_Red_Claws "Maine Red Claws") of the [NBA D-League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_G_League "NBA G League").
Mazzulla was named head coach of Fairmont State in March 2017.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-gaz-16) During his second season, Mazzulla led the team to a 22–9 record and an appearance in the [2019 NCAA Division II tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_NCAA_Division_II_men's_basketball_tournament "2019 NCAA Division II men's basketball tournament"), where they lost in the first round to [Mercyhurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyhurst_Lakers "Mercyhurst Lakers"), 63–60, in overtime.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-20)
### Boston Celtics
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Mazzulla&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Boston Celtics")]
#### Assistant coach
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Mazzulla&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Assistant coach")]
On June 24, 2019, Mazzulla was hired as an assistant coach of the [Boston Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-jackson-17) In 2022, he interviewed with the [Utah Jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_Jazz "Utah Jazz") for their head coaching vacancy, but the position ultimately went to fellow Celtics assistant coach [Will Hardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Hardy "Will Hardy").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-21)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-22)
#### Head coach
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Mazzulla&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Head coach")]
##### 2022–23 season: First season
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Mazzulla&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2022–23 season: First season")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Joe_Mazzulla.png/250px-Joe_Mazzulla.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Joe_Mazzulla.png)Mazzulla in 2022
On September 22, 2022, just days before the beginning of training camp, Mazzulla was named interim head coach for the Celtics after [Ime Udoka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ime_Udoka "Ime Udoka") was suspended for the entire [2022–23 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Boston_Celtics_season "2022–23 Boston Celtics season") due to violating team policies.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-23)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-24) On December 1, Mazzulla was named [Eastern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Conference_\(NBA\) "Eastern Conference \(NBA\)") Coach of the Month for October and November after the Celtics began the season with a league-best 18–4 record.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-25)
On January 30, 2023, Mazzulla was named the head coach for Team [Giannis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giannis_Antetokounmpo "Giannis Antetokounmpo") for the [2023 NBA All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NBA_All-Star_Game "2023 NBA All-Star Game").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-26) A few weeks later on February 16, the Celtics officially named him the 19th head coach in franchise history and signed Mazzulla to a contract extension after he led the team to a league-best 42–17 record at the [NBA All-Star break](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_All-Star_break "NBA All-Star break").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-27)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-28) In April, Mazzulla was named one of three finalists for [NBA Coach of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Coach_of_the_Year "NBA Coach of the Year").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-29) The Celtics entered the playoffs as the #2-seed in the Eastern Conference with a 57–25 record.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-30) They went on to beat the [Atlanta Hawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Hawks "Atlanta Hawks") in six games during the first round and the [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") in seven games during the Eastern Conference Semifinals.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-31)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-32) However, the Celtics lost to the #8-seed [Miami Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Heat "Miami Heat") during the [Eastern Conference Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_conference_finals "NBA conference finals") in seven games, where Boston lost the first three games of the series. Despite losing the series, the Celtics became just the fourth team in league history to force a Game 7 after trailing 3–0 in a playoff series, and the first since the [2002–03 Portland Trail Blazers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002%E2%80%9303_Portland_Trail_Blazers_season "2002–03 Portland Trail Blazers season"). During Game 7, star [Jayson Tatum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayson_Tatum "Jayson Tatum") rolled his ankle less than a minute into the game and played through the injury, but was noticeably hindered for the rest of the game.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-33)
##### 2023–24 season: First NBA Championship
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Mazzulla&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2023–24 season: First NBA Championship")]
Mazzulla was retained as head coach for the [2023–24 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Boston_Celtics_season "2023–24 Boston Celtics season") and received the endorsement of President of Basketball Operations [Brad Stevens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Stevens "Brad Stevens"), who called him "a terrific leader" and "accountable".[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-35)
During the season, Mazzulla earned two Eastern Conference Coach of the Month awards, one in December and another in March.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-36)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-37) With a league-best 64–18 record, the Celtics had their first 60+ win season since 2009 and took the top overall seed in the NBA along with home-court advantage throughout the playoffs for the first time since their [last championship season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Boston_Celtics_season "2007–08 Boston Celtics season").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-38)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-39) The Celtics went on to beat the [Miami Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Heat "Miami Heat") and [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers") in five games during the first round and Eastern Conference Semifinals, respectively.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-40)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-41) After completing a 4–0 sweep of the [Indiana Pacers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_Pacers "Indiana Pacers") in the Eastern Conference Finals,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-42) Mazzulla, at age 35, became the youngest head coach to make the [NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Finals "NBA Finals") since [Bill Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Russell "Bill Russell") in 1969.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-43) The Celtics went on to defeat the [Dallas Mavericks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Mavericks "Dallas Mavericks") in five games during the [2024 NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_Finals "2024 NBA Finals"), giving Mazzulla his first NBA championship.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-44) Mazzulla also became the youngest head coach to win the NBA Finals in over 50 years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-youngest_coach-5)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-45)
##### 2024–25 season
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Mazzulla&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2024–25 season")]
Mazzulla was named Eastern Conference Coach of the Month in March after the Celtics finished the month with a 14–1 record, including a perfect 8–0 record on the road.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-46) They ultimately finished with a 61–21 record to clinch their 26th [Atlantic Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Division_\(NBA\) "Atlantic Division \(NBA\)") and finished as the #2-seed in the East for the playoffs, behind the No. 1 ranked [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_Cleveland_Cavaliers_season "2024–25 Cleveland Cavaliers season").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-47) The Celtics beat the [Orlando Magic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic "Orlando Magic") in five games during the first round,[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-48) but lost to the [New York Knicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Knicks "New York Knicks") in six games during the Eastern Conference Semifinals, which also saw them lose [Jayson Tatum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayson_Tatum "Jayson Tatum") to an [Achilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achilles_tendon "Achilles tendon") injury in Game 4.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-49)
##### 2025–26 season: Contract extension
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Mazzulla&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2025–26 season: Contract extension")]
On August 8, 2025, Mazzulla signed a multi-year extension with the Celtics.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-50)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-51) Despite the absence of [Jayson Tatum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayson_Tatum "Jayson Tatum") for most of the season, they still managed to achieve a 56–26 record to clinch their 27th [Atlantic Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Division_\(NBA\) "Atlantic Division \(NBA\)"), and finish once again as the #2-seed in the East for the playoffs, but this time behind the No. 1 ranked [Detroit Pistons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_Detroit_Pistons_season "2025–26 Detroit Pistons season").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-52) The Celtics went on to lose to the [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") in seven games during the first round despite a 3–1 lead.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-53) On May 26, Mazzulla was named the [NBA Coach of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Coach_of_the_Year "NBA Coach of the Year") for the first time in his career.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-54)
## Personal life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joe_Mazzulla&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Personal life")]
Mazzulla's father, [Dan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Mazzulla "Dan Mazzulla"), was of Sicilian descent[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-bostonglobe00-55) and was a basketball player and coach who died in 2020.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-koch-56) Mazzulla's mother, Latresa, is of African descent.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-bostonglobe00-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-57)[_[unreliable source?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")_] His younger brother, [Justin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Mazzulla "Justin Mazzulla"), played basketball at [George Washington University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington_Revolutionaries_men's_basketball "George Washington Revolutionaries men's basketball") before transferring to the [University of Vermont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vermont_Catamounts_men's_basketball "Vermont Catamounts men's basketball").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-58)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-59) Justin is currently an assistant video coordinator for the [Utah Jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_Jazz "Utah Jazz").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-60) Mazzulla also has a younger sister, Gianna, who played under her father Dan at Johnston High School.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-koch-56)
Mazzulla has been married to Camai Roberson since 2014, whom he met while coaching at Glenville State University in 2011.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-61)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-62) With Robinson, Mazzulla has a son, Emmanuel Joseph Daniel Mazzulla, and a stepson, Michael Harden.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-63)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-64)
Mazzulla is a devout [Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic "Catholic"), saying that his identity comes from his "faith" and "purpose". He has also said his dream would being ordained a [deacon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deacon "Deacon").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-65)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-66)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-67)
Mazzulla is a fan of [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League") club [Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C "Manchester City F.C"), and has developed a friendship with Manchester City's manager, [Pep Guardiola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pep_Guardiola "Pep Guardiola").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-68)
Mazzulla actively trains in [Brazilian jiu-jitsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_jiu-jitsu "Brazilian jiu-jitsu") and has said that the sport helps him navigate life's challenges.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-69) Mazzulla originally began training in 2017, and after becoming head coach of the Celtics five years later, he re-committed to the discipline. Mazzulla has also noted that it helps him connect better with his players.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-70)
Mazzulla is known for having an idiosyncratic personality, possessing interesting quirks that shape both his external communications as well as his coaching philosophy.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-71)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-72)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-73) Mazzulla's similarities to former [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Patriots "New England Patriots") head coach [Bill Belichick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Belichick "Bill Belichick") have been noted by several sources in the media.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mazzulla#cite_note-74)[_[failed verification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] Both tend to be introverted and reserved regarding their teams' successes and weaknesses, and both have a harsh regard for the media along with interesting "quirks" that define them as their personalities.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
